new_findings_confirmed_vs_candidates.chain_4_vs_chain_8_non_monotonic: CONFIRMED at N=2 (R37 + R40). Both runs: vt@16K chain=4 FAIL 0/1, vt@16K chain=8 PASS 1/1. The reasoning ceiling is NOT simply 'chain >= 4'; chain=8 passes while chain=4 fails. Possible explanations: (a) per-instance stochasticity with chain=4 drawing specifically hard problems, (b) chain=4 has a specific failure mode (e.g., specific variable binding pattern), (c) sample size too small (N=1 per task) and chain=8 would also sometimes fail. Needs multi-sample per chain length to distinguish.
new_findings_confirmed_vs_candidates.frequent_word_uniform_33pct: CONFIRMED at N=3 (R35, R37, R40 all show fw@4K/fw@16K at 33%). Pattern is too uniform to be random 1/3-per-task sampling noise. Either a systematic retrieval issue or the test items are built such that 1 of 3 is typically findable.
new_findings_confirmed_vs_candidates.not_filing_as_tasks_yet: Both findings are analytically interesting but not yet actionable.
